findings.note: build-release.sh:265-269 is only a pre-check; publish() at 309-312 uses mv, which silently replaces an existing $out/$1.
release_bundle.rs:463-474 uses substring checks (short is a prefix of the sha= value) and never asserts libc=; a weak informational-file test.

build-release.sh:20 says the environment cannot change codegen, but only RUSTFLAGS/CARGO_BUILD_TARGET are unset (193); RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN overrides rust-toolchain.toml and RUSTC_WRAPPER/CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_* are untouched.
True that no --offline/--frozen is used (194), but REQ-0012 governs req's runtime, not the owner's release build; network on a build host is not a product defect.
Missing tools make the script die 2 naming the tool (150-158), a clear message; a fixture-setup suggestion with no defect.
The 40 bound (220) would reject a SHA-256 object-format repo, but this repo is SHA-1; hypothetical.
The stub prints ${STUB_BUILT_FROM:-unknown} (release_bundle.rs:54), so the String::new() case (544) duplicates "unknown" and the script's empty-value branch (215) is never exercised.
cleanup (66-82) keeps errexit and INT/TERM traps armed; a second signal mid-cleanup could abort it, but this is a narrow edge case.

Without pipefail, line 287's fallback is dead (head's status) so a missing ldd records the shell error text; it only affects the informational libc line, and the sha256 path is caught by the hex check (280-283).
assert_nothing_written (373-384) accepts an empty existing --out, weaker than the header's 'not even created'; a test-strength nit.
Same as F01: publish() at 310-311 mv-replaces an existing destination, so the pre-check at 265-269 is TOCTOU.
asset() (360-363) hardcodes TARGET while World::new takes a host; a maintainability nit with no current failing test.
